races.paceDynamic: Warfleet and Poet's Muse will ensure a genuine gallop from the start, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead. The honest pace will stretch the field and create opportunities for closers to pick up the pieces if the leaders tire. With soft going adding to the stamina test over this extended trip, horses who can produce a sustained finish will have the tactical edge. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses — the pace is genuine and the field will be strung out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace between Warfleet and Poet's Muse is genuinely strong
scenarios.body: The leaders will tire in the soft ground, allowing patient hold-up horses to come through with perfectly timed challenges in the final furlong. Dutch Corner and Hardly Surprising benefit most from this tactical setup.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Limier d'Arthel or Handmedownastar track the pace without getting involved in early battles
scenarios.body: They can avoid the pace duel while staying close enough to strike when the leaders weaken, benefiting from both tactical position and stamina reserves. Philip Hobbs' stable form and Handmedownastar's recent third suggest they're ready to capitalize.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If one of the early leaders gets an easier time by establishing a clear advantage
scenarios.body: Warfleet's higher rating suggests he could dominate if allowed his own way, while the soft ground will test his stamina reserves less severely. His 394-day absence remains a concern but the class edge could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely or the market leaders underperform significantly
scenarios.body: Lower-rated horses like Dante's Rocco or Ask A Sainte could benefit from a muddling pace that neutralizes class differences. Syd Hosie's 3/16 form and David Brace's booking of Finn Lambert suggest stable confidence in their chances.

watchPoints.text: Warfleet's 394-day absence is a major concern despite his front-running style potentially suiting the race shape
JPR Two from Paul Nicholls stable could outrun his poor recent form given the trainer's 3/26 strike rate
Limier d'Arthel's prominent style and Philip Hobbs' excellent 3/14 form make him a key pace indicator
Several horses show concerning fade patterns (Docteur Romeo, Saffron Belle, Mrs Pen) which the soft ground will expose
Dutch Corner's consistent placed form and Dan Skelton's strong 9/40 record suggest he's well-handicapped for this contest

runners_data.name: Palawan Du Mazet

runners_data.name: Tractor Jack

races.paceDynamic: Begin The Luck will set a controlled front pace from the outset, with Firefly Lane, Devilsrollthedice and Tractor Jack sitting in prominent positions behind. The remainder - Ideallko, Jack's A Legend, Jack Doyen and Palawan Du Mazet - are all hold-up horses who will settle in behind and look to come with late runs. With only one confirmed front runner and several prominent runners content to track, the pace will be sustainable rather than frantic. This setup strongly favours hold-up horses - the pace will be genuine enough to set up a finish but not so strong as to compromise closers, and the field composition ensures a strong gallop to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Begin The Luck sets a steady but true gallop and the hold-up horses get the perfect setup
scenarios.body: The pace will be ideal for the closers to unleash their finishing kicks, with the prominent runners having done too much work early. Ideallko's strong recent form and Jack Doyen's class on his lighter weight make them prime beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Control
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too steady and Begin The Luck gets an easy lead with minimal pressure
scenarios.body: The front-runners will have too much left in the tank, making it difficult for the hold-up horses to peg them back up the hill. Begin The Luck's solid soft ground form and Devilsrollthedice's prominent style could prosper.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Begin The Luck goes too slow early and the race becomes a sprint from the last fence
scenarios.body: The race will become tactical and scrappy, suiting horses with natural speed rather than sustained galloping ability. This could bring Palawan Du Mazet's recent winning form into play despite his hold-up style.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Burns Out Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners go too hard trying to pressure Begin The Luck and set up a complete collapse
scenarios.body: The early pace-setters will pay the price for their aggressive tactics, but the hold-up horses may also struggle if the race becomes stop-start. An outsider like Firefly Lane could benefit from the chaos.

watchPoints.text: Begin The Luck's early pace-setting - if he goes too slow the hold-up horses will struggle to make up ground
Jack's A Legend's fitness after 311 days off - any signs of rustiness will compromise his chances despite the confident jockey booking
Tractor Jack's tendency to fade in the finish - monitor if he's travelling strongly turning for home or already under pressure
Ideallko's jumping early on after 59-day break - needs to settle into rhythm quickly to utilize his strong recent form
The pace pressure on Begin The Luck from the prominent runners - whether Firefly Lane, Devilsrollthedice or Tractor Jack apply any early pressure

runners_data.name: Northern Air

runners_data.name: Green Sky

runners_data.comment: Pulled up in last two chases but reverts to hurdling on a dangerous mark
runners_data.spotlight: Close third over hurdles at Chepstow (2m, good) in October but she's not taken to fences this winter and has been pulled up in last two starts; bit to prove but she's on a dangerous mark back in this sphere and could be a big factor if she can revive; blinkers worn in last two starts are removed.

runners_data.name: Parikarma
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose best form comes with cut in ground, though 7-pound claimer Miss Mathias faces a tactical challenge in this pace-less field

runners_data.name: Reel Orange
runners_data.note: Recent improved form with Joe Tizzard's strong 3/24 strike rate, though pull-up two runs back raises stamina questions despite first-time tongue-tie

runners_data.name: Getarose
runners_data.note: Youngest in field with significant weight relief at bottom of handicap, but limited soft ground experience and needs career-best effort

runners_data.name: Eskimo Sam
runners_data.note: Tendency to fade in finish makes him vulnerable in likely sprint finish, though Sean Houlihan booking suggests some stable confidence

races.paceDynamic: With only Green Sky showing any real front-running tendencies in a field of seven hold-up horses, this will be an unusually controlled affair. Green Sky can dictate terms uncontested through the early stages, setting a moderate gallop that suits her patient style. The lack of pace pressure means the field will travel in a tight pack for most of the journey before the real race begins approaching the final flight. This setup strongly favours horses with tactical speed and the ability to quicken — those who can position handily and pounce when Green Sky's soft pace inevitably leads to a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Green Sky sets an uncontested moderate pace throughout
scenarios.body: The field arrives bunched at the last flight creating a cavalry charge finish where horses with the best recent form and tactical speed prosper. Northern Air and Jackeline benefit most from this scenario with their proven ability to quicken off a steady gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Green Sky Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Green Sky's recent front-running tendencies translate to leading throughout and the field fails to close
scenarios.body: Despite her hold-up style rating, she gets an easy lead and David Pipe's mare finds enough to hold off late challengers on the soft ground. Reel Orange from the Joe Tizzard yard could be the main danger having shown improved form lately.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Green Sky fails to go forward leaving no obvious leader among the hold-up horses
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy crawl with multiple horses trying to make the running reluctantly, setting up a chaotic finish. This randomness could suit an outsider like Getarose who gets weight relief, or the returning Parikarma.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Battle Backfires
scenarios.trigger: If jockeys overcook the tactical riding and leave too much to do from the back
scenarios.body: The steady pace becomes genuinely slow and those who position closer benefit while the confirmed hold-up horses find traffic problems. Reel Orange and Northern Air suffer most if they get buried too far back.

watchPoints.text: Northern Air's fitness after 94-day break — if he's sluggish early or fails to travel smoothly the layoff has left its mark
Green Sky's tactical approach — watch if Callum Pritchard sends her forward early or tries to hold her up as usual given the pace scenario
Jackeline's jumping — two recent pull-ups suggest either fitness or confidence issues that could manifest as sketchy hurdling
The pace through halfway — if it's genuinely crawling multiple horses will be in contention turning in creating traffic nightmares
Reel Orange's tongue-tie effect — first-time application suggests breathing issues may have hampered recent efforts

runners_data.name: Bumpy Evans
runners_data.note: Lone leader gets dream scenario but returning from 167-day layoff and trainer has no recent winners to show confidence

races.paceDynamic: Bumpy Evans is the sole confirmed front runner and will have an uncontested lead from the flag, setting a comfortable pace without pressure from the seven prominent runners behind. The large group of P-style horses (Tahmuras, Scarface, Royal Jewel, Calimystic, Nickelforce, Hardy Du Seuil) will settle in a pack, with only Kap Ouest holding up at the back. With no pace pressure early, Bumpy Evans can dictate terms and kick when ready, while the prominent runners will need to time their challenges perfectly from similar positions. This setup strongly favours the lone leader and any horse that can get first run from the pack — the lack of early pace pressure gives the front runner a significant tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bumpy Evans Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Bumpy Evans gets an easy lead and times his kick right
scenarios.body: The 8-year-old can dictate fractions without harassment and has the class (RPR 139) to repel late challengers when they come. His Kerry Lee stable may be quiet (T14: 0/0) but this front-running specialist has won twice from good going and the lack of pace pressure plays perfectly to his strengths.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Battle Decides
scenarios.trigger: If the pack of prominent runners close together and one gets first run
scenarios.body: The seven P-style horses will bunch up behind the leader, creating a cavalry charge finish where positioning and timing matter most. Calimystic's Henderson stable (T14: 3/15) and de Boinville booking suggest confidence, while his lightly raced profile could have more improvement.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Kap Ouest Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint
scenarios.body: Kap Ouest's H-style will benefit if this becomes a slow-run affair where his late kick can be most effective. Harry Fry's 7-year-old has solid form figures (U5-921) and won last time out over this trip in soft ground.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Bumpy Evans goes too slow and gets swamped by multiple challengers
scenarios.body: Without pace pressure, the leader could get caught flat-footed when multiple horses challenge simultaneously. The prominent runners with the highest RPRs (Tahmuras 138, Scarface 138) could prevail in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Bumpy Evans getting loose on the lead — if he builds a big advantage early, the prominent pack may not catch him in time
The gap between Bumpy Evans and the pack at the second-last fence — this will determine if the leader has enough left
Calimystic's position turning for home — Henderson's booking of de Boinville suggests this lightly raced horse has more to offer
How quickly the seven prominent runners bunch up behind the leader — positioning will be crucial in the final furlong
Kap Ouest's progress from the back — if the pace is genuine he could be the each-way value coming from last

races.paceDynamic: Call Me Legend will dictate terms from the front with minimal early pressure in this small field. The prominent runners Striking A Pose, Rickety Bridge and Crossgales King may track but won't hassle early, creating a measured gallop over this marathon trip. Top Guy and Walk Tall as the designated hold-up horses will be patient at the rear, relying on stamina to come home late. This setup moderately favours hold-up horses — the pace will be genuine but controlled, and the soft going will sap the early leaders over this extreme distance.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Call Me Legend sets an honest but not frantic pace and the field strings out over the final mile
scenarios.body: The patient tactics of Top Guy and Walk Tall will pay dividends as they pick off tiring leaders. Dan Skelton's 9/42 strike rate and Top Guy's excellent soft going record (9/10) make him the prime beneficiary.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front runner sustains kick
scenarios.trigger: If Call Me Legend's class tells and he can quicken despite setting the pace throughout
scenarios.body: Philip Hobbs' 3/14 record suggests stable confidence and his recent form (431122) shows consistent performance levels. The 13-day break keeps him fresh for this stamina test.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent tracker strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent runners can secure the ideal position tracking the leader without doing too much work
scenarios.body: Crossgales King's recent win and Syd Hosie's 3/16 record indicate readiness, while his soft going form (7/9) is solid. The race will set up perfectly for a well-positioned stalker.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses early
scenarios.trigger: If Call Me Legend goes too slow early and it becomes a sprint finish
scenarios.body: The marathon distance makes this unlikely but if it happens, the higher-rated horses with tactical speed will benefit. Class will tell in a bunched finish.

watchPoints.text: Call Me Legend could get an uncontested lead if prominent runners are too patient early
Top Guy's soft going form (9/10) makes him the key danger from the rear if pace is strong enough
Crossgales King's 30-day break could be ideal for this stamina test given his recent winning form
Sam's Amour's 99-day absence is significant concern despite trainer booking Sean Houlihan
The 152lb minimum weight for Walk Tall gives him a significant pull at the weights over this extreme trip

runners_data.name: Numero Ventotto

runners_data.spotlight: Third foal; dam bumper winner, sister to 2m3f/2m5f hurdle winner Touchy Feely, closely related to useful bumper and 2m3f-2m7f hurdle/chase winner Sure Touch, out of useful 2m3f/2m5f chase winning close relative of Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Long Run; has a striking pedigree and she's an interesting newcomer for top yard.

runners_data.name: Frenati
runners_data.comment: Narrow win at Stratford but the form does not looks strong; has work to do under penalty
runners_data.spotlight: Weakened on her Doncaster debut in November but she returned from a break with a brave win at Stratford (2m, soft) last month; that was a major step forward but she only won by a nose and the form does not looks strong; has some work to do under a penalty.
